title: The Deposit Step Applied in an Auto Loans Due Day Realignment
content:
The deposit credit in a realignment of the due day on a loan of the Auto Loans line is multiplied by a deposit step. Two readings of the borrower's Personal Checking account settle that step: whether they hold an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes, and whether at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months.

| How many of the two readings hold | Deposit step |
|---|---|
| Both | 2.0 |
| Exactly one | 1.5 |
| Neither | 1.0 |

The deposit step is 2.0 where both of these hold, that the borrower holds an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes and that at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months. It is 1.5 where exactly one of those two holds. It is 1.0 where neither of them holds.

## The step is a multiplier, not a number of days

Where the whole amounts counted in the deposit measure come to 3 days before the step, the three rows above give 6 days, 4.5 days and 3 days respectively.

## How the two readings are taken

The balance reading compares the posted balance on the borrower's active account in the Personal Checking line against the fee-waiver daily balance published for that account's tier. The deposit reading counts recurring deposits posted to that same account over the three months ending on the day of the realignment; exactly 2 meets the reading and 1 does not.
